objective: Independently consumable Ontology assets, scoped L1/L2/L3 usability and controlled specification-only reconstruction verified on a real functional slice and its substantive evolution
levelPolicy: EvoPilot conventions, not industry certification. Level-specific evidence is necessary but does not waive common scope, identity, freshness, access, compatibility or acceptance requirements. Claims apply only to exact reviewed scope and conditions; no graph-size score, averaging or automatic whole-project promotion.

acceptance.requirement: A real independent HTTP consumer discovers, queries and reads an exact published asset without a Runtime Goal/Run or Codex activation; offline export also works. Show that reading changes no business decision, execution or publication state.

acceptance.requirement: Two isolated scopes reject unauthorized cross-scope/private reads and mutations; revoked credentials fail. Exercise configured TLS/non-loopback transport in an isolated environment, bounded queries/rate/output, link/path traversal and malicious asset text. No credentials leak through assets, logs or errors.

Exact asset/dependency/projection digests survive download and offline readback. Pagination uses an explicit snapshot. Tampering, missing dependency, unsupported format, stale cursor, partial export or silent latest-version substitution fails; consumers see any transformation loss.
journeyRefinements: Navigate explicit object, relation, constraint and source references with immutable pins and complete snapshot pagination; disclose ambiguous version selection.

acceptance.requirement: Versioned level definitions and use-case examples agree across owning rules, public docs and installed consumers. Graph size, triple count, model fixture count, technical PASS or adopting RDF/OWL alone cannot assign a level. Industry references are described as related frameworks, not equivalent certifications.

acceptance.requirement: A builder receives only the approved specification projection and pinned allowed dependencies. Attempts to read original source/binaries, prior generated output, hidden oracle data or a delegating reference service fail through files, caches and network. Audit sources remain privately available to reviewers. Source-assisted runs are explicitly labeled and cannot qualify for L3.

The selected installed Agent/build adapter performs real generation, compilation and execution in the allowed environment with identities, inputs, outputs, cost/usage availability and interventions recorded. Unsupported language/tool/provider or missing prerequisites fails before claiming a run; bound budgets terminate without fabricated results.

Duplicate submission, lost response, timeout, cancellation, partial output, process restart and interrupted persistence preserve exact claim/receipt identity. Reconciliation inspects the original attempt without blindly repeating external work; recovery cannot imply success or overwrite failure.

Independent oracle checks outputs, states, errors and side effects against the frozen contract/reference, using agreed tolerances and applicable boundary/concurrency/recovery cases. Deliberately wrong implementations fail, including duplicate effects and premature success. Withheld acceptance remains independent of generator-authored tests.

Two clean independent reconstruction attempts use the same exact specification input and pass every mandatory case, without sharing generated solutions or original implementation context. Preserve all attempts and interventions. Additional Agent/platform compatibility claims require separate actual evidence.

Failed, skipped, missing, unknown, stale, unsupported and synthetic-only required results block verified L3 and dependent completion. Failure reports identify scope, unmet requirement and actionable gap category; correct rejection does not satisfy a positive reconstruction requirement.

A real substantive specification change yields a new asset and reconstruction; new requirements and retained compatibility/migration checks pass. Changed asset/oracle/environment/dependency pins produce a stale/review-required disposition instead of inheriting prior verification. Historical claims remain readable.

HTTP/SDK, Expert and reports agree on target/verified level, scope, exclusions, input mode, evidence and freshness. Actual installed consumer/Host journeys navigate to exact receipts. Rendering and reading cannot dispatch, approve, publish or invent missing explanations.
journeyRefinements: Installed Expert and owner-rendered reports agree with HTTP/SDK on overview, versions, definitions, gaps and evidence.
Natural-language presentation preserves exact bounds and cannot fabricate meaning, mutate owner state or dispatch work.
modelingIntentRefinements: Verify the applicable mandatory modeling-purpose admission, profile, compatibility and presentation requirements in modelingIntentGate; missing evidence blocks completion.

acceptance.requirement: One privately selected real functional slice achieves the initial L3 checks and the substantive evolution check under exact input/environment pins. Project assets are supplemented through normal reviewed versions as needed. A synthetic substitute, source-assisted reconstruction or only a gap report leaves this criterion incomplete.

Public fixtures are explicitly synthetic and exercise at least two isolated namespaces. Public docs demonstrate all levels without private names, source bytes, credentials or actual approval/evidence. Generic criteria apply without project-specific hardcoding.

Upgrade and isolated backup/restore preserve prior native assets, versions, standards, decisions and receipts byte-for-byte. Additive assessments/projections retain original references, unknown historical levels and pending claims. Old readers fail safely where necessary; maintenance never replays work or silently grades old assets.

acceptance.requirement: Verify the accepted v0.7 dependency contracts and exact four-repository candidate. Documentation, standards limits and failure/recovery guidance match delivered behavior.

Every R-ID maps to owned E-IDs and every mandatory fixed variant has current exact-candidate evidence. All applicable pre-release requirements, including the successful real pilot, pass before a separately authorized release. After authorized publication, downloaded-package/readback checks and closure are required; pre-publication status must not claim those post-release checks have passed.

privacyPolicy: Public requirements and synthetic fixtures are generic. Actual real-project identity, scope, source/asset pins, human decisions and acceptance evidence remain private. Do not mutate private assets while recording this plan.
progressPolicy: Planning is accepted; implementation and all acceptance remain unevaluated. No watcher, automatic resumption, installed capability or completed reconstruction is implied.
